# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Important Correction on Civil Registration

One factual correction from the standard framing: Massachusetts **did have town-level vital recording** throughout this period — ordered from as early as 1639. What 1841 created was the first *statewide* collection system (Boston excluded until 1850). The underlying town clerk books predate 1841 and are a real source for 1820–1850. A digitized Berkshire County volume of **"Town Clerk Vital and Town Records," 1761–1850** (image group 004500891, 512 images) exists on FamilySearch — browse-only, not name-indexed.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Formed:** 1761
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Massachusetts, United States
- **Geography:** Berkshire County borders both New York and Vermont — any family near the county line may have generated records on either side of the state line.

---

## Record Types for 1820–1850

### 1. Town Vital Records (Civil)
- **Scope:** Town-level birth, marriage, and death recording was continuous; the 1841 act created a *state* copy, not the original records.
- **FamilySearch collection:** "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890" (collection id 2061550)
- **Berkshire-specific digitized volume:** Image group 004500891 (512 images, 1761–1850) — browse-only, not searchable by name
- **Physical originals:** Held by each individual town clerk
- **Marriage tip:** Intentions were commonly recorded in the **bride's home town**, and also possibly in the groom's town and the couple's residence — search all three towns

### 2. Church Records
- **What's confirmed:** A digitized volume of **Congregational church records for Pittsfield**, Berkshire County, 1791–1850 (image group 004500892, 274 images) — browse-only, not name-indexed
- **State-level collection:** "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (collection id 1921657, ~987,654 persons) overlaps this period
- **Coverage gap:** No church registers for Berkshire towns *other than Pittsfield* were returned by this survey — this does not prove they don't exist; check `catalog_search` or the FamilySearch Wiki for each specific town's congregation
- **Physical records:** Contact each parish/denominational archive directly

### 3. Cemetery Records
- **Online:** [Find A Grave](https://www.findagrave.com/) is the leading resource for transcribed inscriptions; no Berkshire-specific count was confirmed here
- **Physical:** Town sexton/burial books and direct cemetery surveys are the primary source for many stones not yet transcribed online

### 4. Probate Records
- "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991" (collection id 1678901, ~567,890 persons) — spans this period
- Originals held at the county probate court

### 5. Federal Census
- 1820, 1830, 1840, and 1850 censuses fall within this window — standard federal enumerations, not separately confirmed for Berkshire in this survey

### 6. Passenger and Naturalization Records
- "Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891" (collection id 1784312) — relevant if family members arrived through a Massachusetts port
- "Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906" (collection id 1459213)

### 7. Newspaper Records
- [Newspapers.com](https://www.newspapers.com/) (subscription) for marriage/death announcements; no Berkshire-specific title or date range was returned by this survey

### 8. Military Records
- [Fold3](https://www.fold3.com/) and [NARA](https://www.archives.gov/) for military records (national, not Berkshire-specific)

---

## Repository Summary

| Repository | What it holds | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Town vital records, church records, probate, naturalization, passenger lists; browse-only Berkshire volumes | Free |
| Town clerk (per town) | Original birth/marriage/death books | In-person or written request |
| Church/denominational archives | Original baptism/marriage/burial registers | Contact parish directly |
| County courthouse | Probate and land records | In-person or written request |
| Find A Grave | Cemetery inscriptions | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Subscription |

---

## Records NOT Online / Known Gaps

- **No name-searchable index** covers Berkshire town vital records for 1820–1841 — the two digitized volumes are browse-only
- Cemetery inscriptions beyond volunteer-submitted Find A Grave entries require physical survey
- Church registers for towns other than Pittsfield were not found in this survey — search separately by town and denomination
- No confirmed record losses for Berkshire County were returned by the tools in this survey

---

## Research Tips for a Near-Border Family

1. **Don't treat 1841 as the start of records** — town clerk books go back to colonial law. See: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records
2. **Check all three towns for marriage intentions** — bride's home town, groom's home town, and residence
3. **Cross the state lines** — a family near both the New York and Vermont borders may have generated church, land, or probate records just across those lines. Search adjoining New York and Vermont towns as well as Berkshire
4. **Browse, don't search** — the two confirmed Berkshire volumes on FamilySearch are image-only; plan time for page-by-page reading
5. **Identify the specific congregation** — Pittsfield's Congregational register is confirmed; for any other Berkshire town, run a catalog search to locate that town's surviving registers before browsing

One correction up front: the delegation's premise — that "nothing civil exists for these years" because statewide registration began in 1841 — does not hold. Consistent with this, `volume_search` found a digitized Berkshire County volume of "Town Clerk Vital and Town Records" covering 1761–1850 (image group 004500891, 512 images). So town-level vital records are a real, if browse-only, source for this window, alongside church registers and cemetery inscriptions — the guide below covers all three.

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Geography note:** the county borders both New York and Vermont, so any family near the county line likely generated records on both sides of the state line — see Research tips.

## Boundary changes
Not confirmed beyond the 1761 formation date returned by `place_search`; no boundary change during 1820–1850 was surfaced by these tools. Town-level jurisdiction (not county) is what held and holds the original vital and church records.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Town-level recording ordered from 1639 (not universally followed); statewide system from 1841, Boston excluded until 1850 — per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records.
- **What exists for 1820–1850:** Town clerk books, not a state system, are the operative record for this whole window; a digitized Berkshire County volume of "Town Clerk Vital and Town Records," 1761–1850, exists (image group 004500891, 512 images, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable — browse-only).
- **Where held:** Original records remain with the individual town clerk, per the same Wiki page; FamilySearch's filmed copy is browse-only online.
- **Gaps:** Marriage intentions were commonly recorded in the bride's home town, with additional recordings possibly in the groom's town and current residence — check all three towns.

### Church records
- **What exists:** A digitized volume of Congregational church records for Pittsfield, Berkshire County, 1791–1850 (image group 004500892, 274 images, 0% indexed, not full-text searchable — browse-only). `collections_search` at the Massachusetts (state) level also lists "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630-1920" (collection id 1921657, ~987,654 persons, overlapping this period).

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635-1991" (collection id 1678901, ~567,890 persons) appears in `collections_search` at the state level and spans this period.

### Military records

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |

## Records NOT online
No statewide civil vital-record index covers 1820–1841 online (the state system begins in 1841, Boston 1850, per the Wiki page cited above). The town clerk and church volumes found here are digitized but browse-only — not name-searchable. Cemetery inscriptions beyond what a volunteer has submitted to Find A Grave are not online at all; physical burial-ground surveys are the only source for many.

## Research tips
- The statewide vital-registration system begins in 1841, Boston excepted until 1850, but underlying town-level recording was ordered from 1639 — so do not treat 1841 as when records "start"; it is when a *state* copy starts. See https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records.

- The county borders New York and Vermont; search the adjoining New York and Vermont towns' own vital, church and land records as well as Berkshire's — a family that close to a state line plausibly generated records on either side. This survey did not return a Neighboring Counties table (the generic `wiki_place_page` fallback was returned instead of a Berkshire-specific page), so no adjoining county names can be given here; re-run the page fetch to get them.
- The FamilySearch Wiki's getting-started, online-records, research-tips, and Berkshire-specific "home" pages, plus `Massachusetts_Church_Records` and `Massachusetts_Naming_Customs`, all returned only a generic fallback article with no Berkshire- or Massachusetts-specific content in this run — treat this as a coverage gap in the survey, not as evidence those pages don't exist; re-fetch before relying on their absence.
- Use the Congregational church volume for Pittsfield (1791-1850) directly if the family's town is Pittsfield; for any other Berkshire town, no church volume was returned by this survey — check `catalog_search`/the Wiki separately for that town's congregation.

---
This covers Berkshire County, Massachusetts for the years 1820 to 1850, for a family near both the New York and Vermont borders. Massachusetts did not run a single statewide system for births, marriages and deaths until 1841, but each town had already been keeping its own birth-marriage-death books, going back to colonial law, and a digitized (though not name-searchable) set of those town books for Berkshire, plus a Congregational church register for the town of Pittsfield, both survive for this period; cemetery inscriptions and other church registers are the other main source but need in-person or volunteer-site searching since most are not on any website. # Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Parish:** Billy civil parish, partly in the barony of Carey but chiefly in Lower Dunluce barony, poor-law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, province of Ulster — containing the post town of Bushmills.
- **Ecclesiastical note:** Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride parishes; the rectory and vicarage of Billy alone now form the archdeaconry of Connor.
- **Religious presence confirmed:** Presbyterian, Covenanter, and Wesleyan Methodist meeting houses all existed in the parish alongside Church of Ireland and Catholic congregations — consistent with a Presbyterian family in the Bushmills area.

---

## Civil Registration (Vital Records)
Civil registration is **largely irrelevant for 1780–1870**:
- **Protestant marriages:** registered from 1845
- **All births and deaths:** registered from 1864
- **All marriages:** compulsory from 1864

For an ancestor born c.1825, virtually the entire period predates civil registration. **Church registers are the primary source.**

---

## Church Records

### Presbyterian
- Multiple Presbyterian congregations (and a Covenanter meeting house) existed in the parish.
- The national average start date for Presbyterian registers in Ireland is **1830**, though individual congregations may begin earlier or later.
- Presbyterian registers in Ireland **typically lack burial records** — do not expect death/burial entries even where baptism and marriage registers survive.
- **Action required:** Identify the specific Bushmills-area Presbyterian congregation via PRONI's *Guide to Church Records* to confirm that congregation's register start date and whether the register survives.

### Church of Ireland
- Registers began nationally from 1536, but **roughly two-thirds were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire in Dublin** — a documented national loss.
- Surviving content is partly preserved through the **Betham, Crossle, and Thrift genealogical abstracts** (available on FindMyPast).
- Even for a Presbyterian family, search surviving Church of Ireland registers — the FamilySearch Wiki explicitly recommends this, as denominational affiliation and record-keeping did not always align.

### Catholic
- Most rural Catholic parishes did not begin registers until after Catholic Emancipation (1828); some rural north Antrim registers started as late as 1869–1870.
- Catholic registers also **typically lack burial records**.
- Catholic parish boundaries differed from civil/Church of Ireland parish boundaries — the relevant Catholic parish may not be named "Billy."

---

## Census Records
This is a **documented class-wide loss for Ireland**:
- Pre-1821 censuses: none survive nationally.
- 1821–1851 censuses: mostly destroyed (1922 fire or earlier government pulping).
- 1861 and 1871 censuses: destroyed by government order.

**Use land records as substitutes** (see below).

---

## Land Records *(Primary Census Substitutes)*
Both are confirmed for Billy parish and fall squarely in the 1780–1870 window:

| Record | Period | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Tithe Applotment Books** | 1820s | Tax paid to the Church; names occupiers of land by townland |
| **Griffith's Valuation** | 1840s | Property tax valuation; names householders by townland |

These are the best tools for placing a family in a specific townland during the period before civil registration.

---

## Probate Records
- Billy parish's page points to the general Ireland Probate Records article; specific Antrim probate court information was not confirmed in this survey.
- Probate abstracts (wills, administrations, marriage bonds) partly survive through the **Betham, Crossle, and Thrift abstracts** as substitutes for 1922 losses (available on FindMyPast).

---

## Key Record Losses
1. **~Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire** (Dublin) — a national-level loss; Billy's specific register fate is unconfirmed and must be checked at PRONI.
2. **Irish censuses 1821–1871 almost entirely destroyed** — use Tithe Applotment and Griffith's Valuation instead.
3. **Presbyterian and Catholic registers generally lack burial entries** — do not expect to find death/burial records there.

---

## Repository Guide

### Physical Repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI**, 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Microfilm/original church registers for Antrim parishes, land/estate records, probate material | proni@communities-ni.gov.uk; 028 9053 4800 |
| **RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 | Church of Ireland registers and material not microfilmed elsewhere | library@ireland.anglican.org |
| **National Archives of Ireland**, Bishop Street, Dublin 8 | Tithe Applotment originals, Griffith's Valuation originals, probate finding aids | nationalarchives.ie |
| **Local Presbyterian congregation/presbytery** | Original baptism/marriage registers often still held by the church | Identify via PRONI's Guide to Church Records first |

### Online Repositories
| Repository | What to Find | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI Guide to Church Records** (PDF) | Identifies which denominations' registers survive for Bushmills/Billy and in what form | Free — nidirect.gov.uk |
| **NLI Catholic Registers** (registers.nli.ie) | Catholic parish register images | Free |
| **FindMyPast** | Betham/Crossle/Thrift abstracts; Ireland Non-Conformist Births, Baptisms, Burials & Marriages indexes | Subscription |
| **Ancestry** | Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915; Ireland Abstracts of Wills and Marriages | Subscription |

> **Important:** No specific digitized or indexed FamilySearch collection for Billy parish or County Antrim was confirmed by the tools used in this survey. Registers for this parish almost certainly need to be approached through PRONI directly rather than found by searching online.

---

## Research Tips
1. **Start at PRONI's *Guide to Church Records*.** It will tell you definitively which Presbyterian congregation served Bushmills/Billy, what registers survive, and in what form (microfilm or original).
2. **Search Church of Ireland registers too**, even for a Presbyterian family — the FamilySearch Wiki recommends this strategy.
3. **Do not expect Presbyterian burial records** — these are rarely found in Irish Presbyterian registers.
4. **Use Tithe Applotment (1820s) and Griffith's Valuation (1840s)** to place the family by townland — both are confirmed for Billy parish and cover the period around your ancestor's birth c.1825.
5. **Check surrounding civil parishes** if Billy's registers come up empty — Catholic parish boundaries differ from civil/CoI boundaries, so the relevant Catholic register may be filed under a different parish name.
6. **For Church of Ireland losses**, check the Betham, Crossle, and Thrift genealogical abstracts on FindMyPast as a partial substitute.

---

**Summary:** For an ancestor born c.1825 in Billy civil parish, civil registration is of little help — church registers, Tithe Applotment Books, and Griffith's Valuation are the core sources. The critical first step is to consult PRONI's *Guide to Church Records* to identify the specific Bushmills-area Presbyterian congregation and confirm whether its registers survive and from what date.

- **Roman Catholic divisions:** the parish forms part of the district of Coleraine (same page).

Northern Ireland's six counties (including Antrim) remained part of the United Kingdom after 1922, while the rest of Ireland became the Republic; records up to 1922 can appear in archives on both sides of that later division (National Archives of Ireland and PRONI), but this split postdates the 1780–1870 window and does not affect record creation in that period ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)). # Locality Guide: County Cork, Ireland (1830s–1840s)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **County:** Cork, Munster, Ireland (county dates from 1606)
- **Key historical events:** The Great Famine (beginning 1845) drove heavy emigration from Cork, especially through the port of Cobh/Queenstown
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (majority) and Church of Ireland (Anglican)

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration did **not exist** in the 1830s–1840s. It began nationally on **1 January 1864** for births and deaths; non-Catholic (mostly Church of Ireland) marriages were registered from **1845** onward.
- **For this period:** No civil birth, marriage, or death certificates exist — you must use church records instead.

### Church Records *(primary substitute for vital records)*
- **Denominations:** Roman Catholic (majority) and Church of Ireland
- **Record types:** Catholic parish registers hold baptisms and marriages (rarely burials). Many Cork Catholic parishes' registers begin in the 1810s–1830s, though survival varies by parish.
- **Where held:** The **National Library of Ireland** holds free online digital images of Catholic registers up to 1880. Church of Ireland registers are held by the **Representative Church Body Library** and in local custody.
- **Gap:** Which specific Cork parishes have surviving registers must be checked parish-by-parish at the NLI's own catalogue.

### Census Substitutes *(actual census records destroyed)*
- **1922 Four Courts fire:** Pre-1901 Irish censuses (including the 1841 census directly covering your period) were largely destroyed in the 1922 Dublin fire.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Lists occupiers of tithe-liable land — a census substitute covering the *exact* target decade.
- **Griffith's Valuation (early 1850s):** Lists every householder; slightly post-dates the target window but very close to it, and is the best substitute for the missing 1841/1851 censuses.

### Land Records
- Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) serve as both a land record and census substitute for this period.

### Wills & Probate
- Many wills and government records were also destroyed in the 1922 Four Courts fire. What, if anything, survives for Cork wills of the 1830s–1840s could not be confirmed from this survey — treat this as an open research gap.

### Immigration/Emigration Records *(especially relevant for an emigrant ancestor)*
- **Port:** Cobh/Queenstown, County Cork was a major Famine-era emigration port.
- **Record type:** Passenger manifests for departures from Cork.
- **Important tip:** These manifests list complete family groups, including young children — examine the entire manifest, not just the head of household.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What It Holds | Access |
|---|---|---|
| National Library of Ireland | Digital images of Catholic parish registers up to 1880 | Free online |
| Representative Church Body Library | Church of Ireland (Anglican) parish registers | Contact repository |
| FamilySearch Catalog (Cork, Ireland) | Tithe Books, Griffith's, various Cork collections | Check directly — specific collection IDs not confirmed by this survey's tools |

---

## Known Record Losses
- **1922 Four Courts fire** destroyed most pre-1901 Irish census returns and many wills/government records.
- **Tithe Applotment Books** and **Griffith's Valuation** are the accepted substitutes for the lost censuses.

---

## Research Tips
1. **Go straight to church registers** — there are no civil vital records for the 1830s–1840s.
2. **Use the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837)** as your primary census substitute for the target decade, and Griffith's Valuation for the early 1850s.
3. **A late-1840s non-Catholic marriage** may have a civil record, since non-Catholic marriage registration began in 1845.
4. **For the emigration itself**, passenger manifests from the port of Cobh name the whole family — check for all family members, not just the ancestor you're tracking.
5. **FamilySearch Catalog** for "Cork, Ireland" should be checked directly — this survey's tools did not return specific collection IDs or catalog entries for Cork, which is a known gap in this survey rather than evidence that FamilySearch holds nothing.

---

**In summary:** Researchers tracing a County Cork ancestor in the 1830s–1840s should focus on Catholic or Church of Ireland parish registers (the main substitute for the civil vital records that didn't yet exist), plus the Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation for census information, keeping in mind that the 1922 fire eliminated most other pre-1901 Irish records. If the ancestor emigrated from Cobh, ship passenger lists are an important source that names the entire family group.

Here is the locality guide produced and saved to your project (as **loc_001**):

---

## Lincolnshire, England — Christenings & Marriages, 1750–1800

**Key finding:** England had no civil registration during this period — the Church of England parish registers are the **only** source for christenings and marriages. Most of Lincolnshire's roughly **1,066 digitized parish-register volumes** for these years on FamilySearch are **not name-indexed** and must be browsed image by image.

### Where to Search

| Repository / Site | What it offers |
|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** (indexed collections) | Some parish registers are indexed; unindexed volumes require page-by-page image browsing |
| **Findmypast** | Name-searchable index covering many Lincolnshire parish registers |
| **Ancestry** | Additional indexed coverage of the same registers |
| **FreeReg** | Free name-searchable transcriptions of parish christenings and marriages |
| **Joiner's Marriage Index** | Specialist index for Lincolnshire marriages |
| **Lincolnshire Archives** | Holds the original paper registers (parish copy) |
| **The National Archives** | Related probate and manorial records |

### Strategy Notes
- Each register typically exists in **two copies**: the parish copy and a bishop's transcript sent annually — both are worth checking.
- Name spelling varied greatly; always search **sound-alike variants**.
- The original registers are at **Lincolnshire Archives**; the bishop's transcripts may differ in detail.

### Recommended Next Step
Use **research-plan** to build a sequenced search plan targeting christenings and marriages across Lincolnshire's parishes for 1750–1800, drawing on this guide to prioritize indexed collections first, then image browsing for the gaps.

quirks: England, Births and Christenings 1538-1975; England Marriages 1538-1973; England Deaths and Burials 1538-1991; and the Great Britain equivalent collections are all Legacy Collections at FamilySearch — partial indexes assembled around April 2010, no longer added to or corrected; verify any hit against the original parish register image. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records

Church of England marriage records after 1753 (Hardwicke's Marriage Act) show residence, marital status, banns/license, witnesses and the minister's name; before 1754 entries are typically bare name-and-date only — do not expect the richer fields before that date. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records

Civil registration (GRO) did not begin until 1 July 1837 — for 1750-1800 there is no civil registration at all; parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials) are the only vital-event source for this window. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration

Surnames and given names in this period had no standardized spelling and were recorded phonetically — search variant spellings; FamilySearch's own 'English Phonetic surname Aliases 1750 to 1800' article is built specifically for this date range. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Naming_Customs

England adopted the Gregorian calendar in September 1752 (11 days skipped) and moved New Year's Day from 25 March to 1 January — pre-1752 dates in the 1750-1800 window need double-dating care. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records

Most of the 1,066 Lincolnshire parish-register volumes found for 1750-1800 are browse-only images (no name index) — of the Marriage group only 3 of 323 volumes are fulltext/indexed, the rest must be browsed page by page; same pattern for Baptism (4 of 650 fulltext) and Religious/Burial groups (0 indexed).

Lincolnshire parish registers are also indexed by several non-FamilySearch sites (Joiner's Marriage Index covering 110 Lincolnshire parishes, FreeReg, Lincolnshire Family History Society) — check these alongside FamilySearch since FamilySearch's own coverage is largely unindexed for this period.

args.guideSection:
## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Lincolnshire is an ancient maritime county in eastern England, bounded by the Humber (N/NE, separating it from Yorkshire), the German Ocean/North Sea (E), Norfolk (SE), Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire (S), Rutlandshire (SW), Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire (W), and Yorkshire (NW). It was historically divided into three Parts — Holland, Kesteven, and Lindsey — each containing several wapentakes, and contained 620 parishes plus 43 extra-parochial places. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy
- **County town:** Lincoln (the city of Lincoln sits within the Parts of Lindsey)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** England, United Kingdom; FamilySearch's own `place_search` only resolves a standard place for Lincolnshire dated "+1801/" onward, so earlier-period records are catalogued under the same county name without a distinct pre-1801 standard place.
- **Religious composition (1851 count, retrospective but indicative of the area's long-standing Nonconformist strength):** 657 Church of England places of worship, 462 Wesleyan Methodist, 221 Primitive Methodist, 38 Independent, 22 Particular Baptist, 31 New Connexion General Baptist, 9 Quaker, 13 Roman Catholic, among others. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy (quoting Wilson's *Imperial Gazetteer of England and Wales*, 1870-72)
- **Research unit:** Genealogy records in England, including Lincolnshire, are kept at the parish level, not the county level — the county page exists mainly to organize access to parish-level record sets. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Getting_Started

args.guideSection:
## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** National civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths in England and Wales began 1 July 1837 — there is no civil registration for the 1750-1800 target window at all. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration
- **What exists for 1750-1800:** None (civil); the parish is the only registration authority in this period (see Church records below).
- **Where held:** Not applicable for this period.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church of England parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials) and nonconformist chapel registers are the sole vital-event sources for 1750-1800.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England (established, state church since the 1530s) is overwhelmingly dominant in Lincolnshire parish record-keeping for this period; Wesleyan and Primitive Methodist, Independent, Baptist, Quaker, and Roman Catholic congregations were also active in the county (per the 1851 count above), though most nonconformist registers for 1750-1800 are thinner and scattered. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy
- **Record types:** Parish registers of baptisms, marriages, and burials; separate banns registers from 1754; bishop's transcripts (BTs, annual copies sent to the bishop/archdeacon, required since 1598 and continuing through this period to about 1870); parish chest records (vestry minutes, poor law/settlement/removal records, apprenticeship indentures). Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records
- **Where held:** `volume_search` found 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire volumes overlapping 1750-1800 across Vital/Religious/Baptism/Marriage/Death/Cemetery groups (e.g. imageGroupNumber 007566004_002_M921-DG2 for Kirkby Green marriages 1722-1812; 007565995 series for Old Somerby baptisms/marriages/burials 1730-1812). The great majority are **browse-only images** — of 323 Marriage-group volumes only 1 is fulltext-searchable, of 650 Baptism-group volumes only 4, and the 519 Religious Marriage and 434 Religious Death volumes have none indexed or fulltext. Originals are deposited at county record offices (Lincolnshire Archives) per standard England practice. Source: volume_search; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records
- **Gaps:** No specific register-loss finding for Lincolnshire came back from any tool in this survey; absence from an index is a digitization gap, not proof the register does not survive.
- **Language:** English (with some Latin terms/abbreviations common in pre-1700 entries carrying into early-18th-century registers; this survey found no Latin-register requirement specific to Lincolnshire for 1750-1800).

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** The first UK census was 1801 (headcounts only, no names); the earliest genealogically useful named census is 1841. Neither falls in the 1750-1800 target window — census is background only for this project.
- **Other enumerations:** Protestation Returns of 1641-1642 and Hearth Tax lists predate the window; this survey did not find evidence of a Lincolnshire-specific census substitute in 1750-1800. Use poor law and settlement records (below) as the household-level substitute for this period.
- **Access:** Not applicable to target window for census proper.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, inventories — jurisdiction depended on the deceased's property: the Prerogative Court of Canterbury (PCC) handled estates with property in more than one diocese: 1384-1858 PCC will registers are indexed at Ancestry/MyHeritage. Source: external_links_search results.
- **Testate or intestate:** Determine which applies to the individual before choosing a series — wills go to PCC/diocesan consistory court indexes, administrations (no will) to the same courts' administration bonds.
- **Date range:** Covers the full 1750-1800 window via PCC indexes (1384-1858).
- **Where held:** The National Archives (PCC originals); diocesan/consistory court probate for lower-value estates would be in Lincolnshire's own diocesan record office (this survey did not confirm the exact Lincoln consistory court holdings).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes-and-bounds / manorial, typical of pre-Ordnance-Survey England.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** This survey did not confirm a Lincolnshire-specific land office; manorial records are centrally indexed via The National Archives' Manorial Documents Register. Source: external_links_search ("Manorial Documents Register, The National Archives" link returned in England Online Records).
- **Types:** Deeds, manorial court rolls, enclosure awards (Lincolnshire underwent extensive parliamentary enclosure in the later 18th century, though this survey found no tool-sourced count of Lincolnshire enclosure acts).
- **Where held:** County record office (Lincolnshire Archives) for deeds/enclosure awards; The National Archives for manorial documents register entries.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Seven Years' War (1756-1763), American War of Independence (1775-1783), and the opening years of the French Revolutionary Wars (from 1793) all fall in this window.
- **Record types:** Army/Navy service and pension records; Chelsea Pensioners' Service Records 1760-1913 (index & images, FamilySearch collection 1952868) and British Royal Navy Ships' Musters 1739-1861 are both within range. Source: collections_search, wiki_place_page (online_records)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch/Ancestry/Findmypast indexes as above; originals at The National Archives.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not itemized by name in any tool result for Lincolnshire; "monumental inscriptions" (England's term for tombstones) are covered by a dedicated findmypast collection, **Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions, 1400s-2000s**. Source: external_links_search
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (general, undated); the Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions collection above spans the target period.
- **Physical records:** Burial registers themselves are the Church records above, not separate sexton records, for this period.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** This survey did not confirm specific Lincolnshire newspaper titles or date ranges for 1750-1800; no tool result named one.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (general UK resource) was returned by external_links_search as a national-level link, not Lincolnshire-specific.
- **Content value:** Marriage/death notices for the gentry tend to predate wide newspaper coverage of ordinary parish families in this era; treat as a supplementary, not primary, source for christenings/marriages of ordinary families.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not a Lincolnshire research priority for christenings/marriages; included for completeness. Lincolnshire has North Sea coastline but no tool result named a specific port of entry/emigration record set for this county and period.
- **Record types:** General England emigration indexes (e.g. Emigrants in Bondage 1614-1775) returned by external_links_search are national in scope, not county-specific.
- **Where held:** Not confirmed for Lincolnshire specifically.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Poor rate / land tax assessments, found in parish chest records.
- **Date range:** Parish chest records generally run from the late 18th or early 19th century in many parishes, per England Church Records' general note that many parish chest series don't begin until then — check survival parish by parish.
- **Where held:** County record office (Lincolnshire Archives), alongside parish registers.
- **Substitute value:** Poor Law removal, settlement certificate, and settlement examination records — Lincolnshire-specific indexed sets at findmypast cover exactly this period: **Lincolnshire Poor Law Removals, 1665-1865**; **Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates, 1675-1860**; **Lincolnshire Settlement Examinations, 1721-1861**. These name individuals and families not otherwise in parish registers and substitute for the absence of civil registration/census in this era. Source: external_links_search

### Other record types
- **Apprenticeship records:** Lincolnshire Parish Apprentice Index, 1618-1925, and Lincolnshire Parish Bastardy Cases, both at findmypast, fall within the target window and are useful substitutes for family-reconstruction work. Source: external_links_search

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England, Births and Christenings 1538-1975 (index only, Legacy); England Marriages 1538-1973 (index only, Legacy); England, Deaths and Burials 1538-1991 (index only, Legacy); 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire parish-register volumes 1750-1800 (mostly browse-only) | Covers christenings/marriages indexes county-wide but as a partial Legacy index only — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records | Free |
| Findmypast | Lincolnshire Parish Registers, 1538-1911 (browse); Lincolnshire Marriages and Banns, 1754-1837 (indexed, directly covers the 1754-1800 banns-era window); Lincolnshire Baptisms; Lincolnshire Burials; Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions, 1400s-2000s; Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates/Examinations/Poor Law Removals | Fills the gap left by FamilySearch's unindexed browse-only volumes with name-searchable Lincolnshire-specific indexes — https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/lincolnshire-marriages-and-banns | Subscription ($) |
| Ancestry | Lincolnshire, England Extracted Church of England Parish Records, 1500s-1800s | Fills the same christening/marriage/burial gap via a separate extraction project — https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/5900 | Subscription ($) |
| Joiner's Marriage Index | 110 Lincolnshire parishes indexed for marriages | Fills the marriage-indexing gap outside FamilySearch/Findmypast for a named subset of parishes — http://joinermarriageindex.co.uk/marriage-records/Lincolnshire/ | Free |
| FreeReg | Transcribed parish register entries (baptisms, marriages, burials), county coverage varies by parish | Free alternative index to subscription sites for parish-register entries — https://www.freereg.org.uk/ | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 1,066 digitized volumes matched Lincolnshire for 1750-1800 in `volume_search`; this guide details only the 10 returned on the first page (imageGroupNumbers above) — the remaining volumes were not individually examined. The `collections_search` call for Lincolnshire returned only 5 UK-wide (not Lincolnshire-specific) collections, confirming that FamilySearch's named/indexed Lincolnshire christening and marriage coverage for this period is thin and that the county's parish-register material is mostly reachable only by image browsing or through the third-party indexes above.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Lincolnshire Archives | Original parish registers, bishop's transcripts, land/enclosure records, probate and poor law records for the county | In-person; online catalogue at http://www.calmview.eu/lincolnshirearchives/calmview/default.aspx |
| The National Archives (Kew) | Prerogative Court of Canterbury wills/administrations; nonconformist registers surrendered under the 1837/1858 Acts; Manorial Documents Register | In-person or online finding aids/orders |
| Lincolnshire Family History Society | Transcriptions and surname indexes (1841-1891 censuses, Nottinghamshire marriage license abstracts with Lincolnshire references, poll tax indexes) held on microfiche, catalogued in the FamilySearch Catalog | In-person at FamilySearch Library (fiche) or via the society — https://www.lincolnshirefhs.org.uk/ |

## Records NOT online

# Locality Guide: Lincolnshire, England, United Kingdom (1750-1800)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Lincolnshire is an ancient maritime county in eastern England, bounded by the Humber (N/NE, separating it from Yorkshire), the German Ocean/North Sea (E), Norfolk (SE), Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire (S), Rutlandshire (SW), Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire (W), and Yorkshire (NW). It was historically divided into three Parts — Holland, Kesteven, and Lindsey — each containing several wapentakes, and contained 620 parishes plus 43 extra-parochial places. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy
- **County town:** Lincoln (the city of Lincoln sits within the Parts of Lindsey)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** England, United Kingdom; FamilySearch's own `place_search` only resolves a standard place for Lincolnshire dated "+1801/" onward, so earlier-period records are catalogued under the same county name without a distinct pre-1801 standard place.
- **Religious composition (1851 count, retrospective but indicative of the area's long-standing Nonconformist strength):** 657 Church of England places of worship, 462 Wesleyan Methodist, 221 Primitive Methodist, 38 Independent, 22 Particular Baptist, 31 New Connexion General Baptist, 9 Quaker, 13 Roman Catholic, among others. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy (quoting Wilson's *Imperial Gazetteer of England and Wales*, 1870-72)
- **Research unit:** Genealogy records in England, including Lincolnshire, are kept at the parish level, not the county level — the county page exists mainly to organize access to parish-level record sets. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Getting_Started

## Boundary changes
This survey found no evidence of county boundary changes affecting Lincolnshire during 1750-1800. The pre-1974 county boundaries (used throughout the FamilySearch Wiki and Catalog) are stable across this window. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Getting_Started. Note the county is itself divided for research purposes into many ancient parishes and chapelries, each of which may hold its own separate register series — a parish/chapelry-level search is still required within the county.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** National civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths in England and Wales began 1 July 1837 — there is no civil registration for the 1750-1800 target window at all. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration
- **What exists for 1750-1800:** None (civil); the parish is the only registration authority in this period (see Church records below).
- **Where held:** Not applicable for this period.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church of England parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials) and nonconformist chapel registers are the sole vital-event sources for 1750-1800.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England (established, state church since the 1530s) is overwhelmingly dominant in Lincolnshire parish record-keeping for this period; Wesleyan and Primitive Methodist, Independent, Baptist, Quaker, and Roman Catholic congregations were also active in the county (per the 1851 count above), though most nonconformist registers for 1750-1800 are thinner and scattered. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy
- **Record types:** Parish registers of baptisms, marriages, and burials; separate banns registers from 1754; bishop's transcripts (BTs, annual copies sent to the bishop/archdeacon, required since 1598 and continuing through this period to about 1870); parish chest records (vestry minutes, poor law/settlement/removal records, apprenticeship indentures). Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records
- **Where held:** `volume_search` found 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire volumes overlapping 1750-1800 across Vital/Religious/Baptism/Marriage/Death/Cemetery groups (e.g. imageGroupNumber 007566004_002_M921-DG2 for Kirkby Green marriages 1722-1812; 007565995 series for Old Somerby baptisms/marriages/burials 1730-1812). The great majority are **browse-only images** — of 323 Marriage-group volumes only 1 is fulltext-searchable, of 650 Baptism-group volumes only 4, and the 519 Religious Marriage and 434 Religious Death volumes have none indexed or fulltext. Originals are deposited at county record offices (Lincolnshire Archives) per standard England practice. Source: volume_search; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Church_Records
- **Gaps:** No specific register-loss finding for Lincolnshire came back from any tool in this survey; absence from an index is a digitization gap, not proof the register does not survive.
- **Language:** English (with some Latin terms/abbreviations common in pre-1700 entries carrying into early-18th-century registers; this survey found no Latin-register requirement specific to Lincolnshire for 1750-1800).

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** The first UK census was 1801 (headcounts only, no names); the earliest genealogically useful named census is 1841. Neither falls in the 1750-1800 target window — census is background only for this project.
- **Other enumerations:** Protestation Returns of 1641-1642 and Hearth Tax lists predate the window; this survey did not find evidence of a Lincolnshire-specific census substitute in 1750-1800. Use poor law and settlement records (below) as the household-level substitute for this period.
- **Access:** Not applicable to target window for census proper.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, inventories — jurisdiction depended on the deceased's property: the Prerogative Court of Canterbury (PCC) handled estates with property in more than one diocese: 1384-1858 PCC will registers are indexed at Ancestry/MyHeritage. Source: external_links_search results.
- **Testate or intestate:** Determine which applies to the individual before choosing a series — wills go to PCC/diocesan consistory court indexes, administrations (no will) to the same courts' administration bonds.
- **Date range:** Covers the full 1750-1800 window via PCC indexes (1384-1858).
- **Where held:** The National Archives (PCC originals); diocesan/consistory court probate for lower-value estates would be in Lincolnshire's own diocesan record office (this survey did not confirm the exact Lincoln consistory court holdings).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes-and-bounds / manorial, typical of pre-Ordnance-Survey England.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** This survey did not confirm a Lincolnshire-specific land office; manorial records are centrally indexed via The National Archives' Manorial Documents Register. Source: external_links_search ("Manorial Documents Register, The National Archives" link returned in England Online Records).
- **Types:** Deeds, manorial court rolls, enclosure awards (Lincolnshire underwent extensive parliamentary enclosure in the later 18th century, though this survey found no tool-sourced count of Lincolnshire enclosure acts).
- **Where held:** County record office (Lincolnshire Archives) for deeds/enclosure awards; The National Archives for manorial documents register entries.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Seven Years' War (1756-1763), American War of Independence (1775-1783), and the opening years of the French Revolutionary Wars (from 1793) all fall in this window.
- **Record types:** Army/Navy service and pension records; Chelsea Pensioners' Service Records 1760-1913 (index & images, FamilySearch collection 1952868) and British Royal Navy Ships' Musters 1739-1861 are both within range. Source: collections_search, wiki_place_page (online_records)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch/Ancestry/Findmypast indexes as above; originals at The National Archives.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not itemized by name in any tool result for Lincolnshire; "monumental inscriptions" (England's term for tombstones) are covered by a dedicated findmypast collection, **Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions, 1400s-2000s**. Source: external_links_search
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (general, undated); the Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions collection above spans the target period.
- **Physical records:** Burial registers themselves are the Church records above, not separate sexton records, for this period.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** This survey did not confirm specific Lincolnshire newspaper titles or date ranges for 1750-1800; no tool result named one.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (general UK resource) was returned by external_links_search as a national-level link, not Lincolnshire-specific.
- **Content value:** Marriage/death notices for the gentry tend to predate wide newspaper coverage of ordinary parish families in this era; treat as a supplementary, not primary, source for christenings/marriages of ordinary families.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not a Lincolnshire research priority for christenings/marriages; included for completeness. Lincolnshire has North Sea coastline but no tool result named a specific port of entry/emigration record set for this county and period.
- **Record types:** General England emigration indexes (e.g. Emigrants in Bondage 1614-1775) returned by external_links_search are national in scope, not county-specific.
- **Where held:** Not confirmed for Lincolnshire specifically.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Poor rate / land tax assessments, found in parish chest records.
- **Date range:** Parish chest records generally run from the late 18th or early 19th century in many parishes, per England Church Records' general note that many parish chest series don't begin until then — check survival parish by parish.
- **Where held:** County record office (Lincolnshire Archives), alongside parish registers.
- **Substitute value:** Poor Law removal, settlement certificate, and settlement examination records — Lincolnshire-specific indexed sets at findmypast cover exactly this period: **Lincolnshire Poor Law Removals, 1665-1865**; **Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates, 1675-1860**; **Lincolnshire Settlement Examinations, 1721-1861**. These name individuals and families not otherwise in parish registers and substitute for the absence of civil registration/census in this era. Source: external_links_search

### Other record types
- **Apprenticeship records:** Lincolnshire Parish Apprentice Index, 1618-1925, and Lincolnshire Parish Bastardy Cases, both at findmypast, fall within the target window and are useful substitutes for family-reconstruction work. Source: external_links_search

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England, Births and Christenings 1538-1975 (index only, Legacy); England Marriages 1538-1973 (index only, Legacy); England, Deaths and Burials 1538-1991 (index only, Legacy); 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire parish-register volumes 1750-1800 (mostly browse-only) | Covers christenings/marriages indexes county-wide but as a partial Legacy index only — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records | Free |
| Findmypast | Lincolnshire Parish Registers, 1538-1911 (browse); Lincolnshire Marriages and Banns, 1754-1837 (indexed, directly covers the 1754-1800 banns-era window); Lincolnshire Baptisms; Lincolnshire Burials; Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions, 1400s-2000s; Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates/Examinations/Poor Law Removals | Fills the gap left by FamilySearch's unindexed browse-only volumes with name-searchable Lincolnshire-specific indexes — https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/lincolnshire-marriages-and-banns | Subscription ($) |
| Ancestry | Lincolnshire, England Extracted Church of England Parish Records, 1500s-1800s | Fills the same christening/marriage/burial gap via a separate extraction project — https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/5900 | Subscription ($) |
| Joiner's Marriage Index | 110 Lincolnshire parishes indexed for marriages | Fills the marriage-indexing gap outside FamilySearch/Findmypast for a named subset of parishes — http://joinermarriageindex.co.uk/marriage-records/Lincolnshire/ | Free |
| FreeReg | Transcribed parish register entries (baptisms, marriages, burials), county coverage varies by parish | Free alternative index to subscription sites for parish-register entries — https://www.freereg.org.uk/ | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 1,066 digitized volumes matched Lincolnshire for 1750-1800 in `volume_search`; this guide details only the 10 returned on the first page (imageGroupNumbers above) — the remaining volumes were not individually examined. The `collections_search` call for Lincolnshire returned only 5 UK-wide (not Lincolnshire-specific) collections, confirming that FamilySearch's named/indexed Lincolnshire christening and marriage coverage for this period is thin and that the county's parish-register material is mostly reachable only by image browsing or through the third-party indexes above.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Lincolnshire Archives | Original parish registers, bishop's transcripts, land/enclosure records, probate and poor law records for the county | In-person; online catalogue at http://www.calmview.eu/lincolnshirearchives/calmview/default.aspx |
| The National Archives (Kew) | Prerogative Court of Canterbury wills/administrations; nonconformist registers surrendered under the 1837/1858 Acts; Manorial Documents Register | In-person or online finding aids/orders |
| Lincolnshire Family History Society | Transcriptions and surname indexes (1841-1891 censuses, Nottinghamshire marriage license abstracts with Lincolnshire references, poll tax indexes) held on microfiche, catalogued in the FamilySearch Catalog | In-person at FamilySearch Library (fiche) or via the society — https://www.lincolnshirefhs.org.uk/ |

subagents.description: Locality guide for Württemberg Lutheran records

output.text_response:
The locality guide has been produced and saved to the project as **loc_001**. Here is a summary of the key findings:

---

## Locality Guide: Lutheran Church-Book Records, Württemberg, Germany, 1780–1830

**Record landscape**
Württemberg had no civil registration in this period — the state didn't require secular birth, marriage, and death registration until 1876. For 1780–1830, **Lutheran parish registers (Kirchenbücher)** are the essential and primary source for baptisms and marriages.

**Where the records are held**
- **Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart (LKAS)** — the principal custodian of Württemberg Lutheran church books; holds original and microfilmed registers from parishes across the kingdom.
- **Archion** (archion.de) — a paid subscription site that provides digitized images of Württemberg Lutheran registers, browsable by parish. This is the main online access point.
- **FamilySearch** — holds some Württemberg Lutheran microfilms (LDS filming), partly digitized as browsable image volumes; coverage is uneven.
- **Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg** — may hold civil or administrative duplicates for some parishes.

**How the records are organized**
Württemberg registers are arranged by **parish (Pfarrei)**, not by county or civil jurisdiction. You must know (or determine) the specific parish village to find the right register.

**Double given-name caution — critical for this family**
Children baptized in Württemberg in this era were routinely given **two given names**, but commonly used the **second** name in daily life and in later records. Record searches must check **both** names (e.g., a child baptized "Johann Friedrich" may appear in later records only as "Friedrich"). Index searches that match only on the first name will miss these individuals.

**What registers typically contain**
- *Taufbücher* (baptism registers): child's given names, date of baptism, father's name and occupation, mother's name, witnesses (Taufpaten/godparents).
- *Heiratsbücher* (marriage registers): groom and bride names, dates, witnesses, sometimes parents' names.
- *Totenbücher* (burial registers): name, date, sometimes age or parents.

**Access strategy**
Because these registers are largely **unindexed digitized images**, searching requires either:
1. Browsing images page by page on Archion (by parish), or
2. Ordering/viewing LDS microfilms through FamilySearch (some volumes are digitized).

A name search alone will not surface results — the parish of origin must be identified first.

**Next step**
Build a research plan targeting the specific parish's Lutheran baptism and marriage registers via Archion or FamilySearch image volumes, checking both given names for every child in the family.

quirks: FamilySearch organizes German records in the Catalog by the place name used in Meyer's Gazetteer at German unification in 1871 — search the FamilySearch Catalog under the 1871 parish/town name even for 1780-1830 events (Württemberg, Germany Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).

Children in this era and region were commonly baptized with two or more given names; which one the person actually went by (often the second name) varied by locality and time — do not assume the first-listed name is the name used in later life (Germany Naming Customs, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Naming_Customs).

Family registers (Familienbücher) recording whole family groups — birth/marriage/death of husband, wife, and children in one record — are especially common in Württemberg and Baden after 1808; check these alongside baptism/marriage registers (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).

Duplicate church-book copies (Kirchenbuchduplikate), most beginning in the late 18th century and required more systematically after 1812, are held in central church or state archives, not the local parish — use them to fill gaps or illegible entries in the original register (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).

Civil registration did not apply in Württemberg for 1780-1830 (it was not under French annexation); church registers remain the primary vital-record source there until the 1876 Empire-wide civil registration requirement (Germany Civil Registration, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration).

args.guideSection:
## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** As a county (Grafschaft) from 1135; elevated to Duchy in 1495; the Kingdom of Württemberg from 1806. For FamilySearch Catalog purposes, German records are organized by the place name used at German unification in 1871 (place_search_all; Württemberg, Germany Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).
- **County seat / administrative center:** Stuttgart
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Holy Roman Empire to 1806, then the Kingdom of Württemberg (within the Confederation of the Rhine, then the German Confederation) through 1830; part of the modern state of Baden-Württemberg since 1952.
- **Population during period:** No Württemberg-specific figures were returned; FamilySearch's population tool gave only country-level Germany estimates for this period (c. 18.0 million in 1800 rising to c. 28.0 million by 1830 — Gapminder data via place_population).
- **Religious denominations:** Predominantly Lutheran (Evangelisch), with Catholic and Reformed minority populations; separate record series were kept by denomination (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Key historical events:** Napoleonic Wars reorganized the territory into the Kingdom of Württemberg (1806); areas west of the Rhine under French control saw civil registration introduced, but Württemberg itself (east of the Rhine) was not annexed and did not adopt civil registration in this period — church registers remained the primary vital-record system (Germany Civil Registration, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration).

args.guideSection:
### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Württemberg is not listed among the areas where Napoleonic-period civil registration (1798-1815) was instituted, and it is not listed among the states that registered before the Empire-wide requirement; statewide civil registration for Württemberg therefore began only with the Empire-wide law of 1 January 1876 (Germany Civil Registration, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration). For 1780-1830, there is no civil-registration series to search.
- **What exists:** None for this window; civil birth/marriage/death registers (Standesamtsregister) begin only in 1876.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Lutheran (and Catholic/Reformed) church registers are the vital-record system for this period — see Church records below.

args.guideSection:
### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Lutheran (Evangelisch) churches began requiring registers around 1540; Catholic parish records were mandated in 1563; Reformed parishes mostly by 1650 (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Württemberg was predominantly Lutheran.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (Taufen) — infant's name, parents' names, legitimacy status, witnesses/godparents, baptism date, sometimes birth date and father's occupation; Marriages (Heiraten) — date, bride/groom names, sometimes ages, birthplaces, parents' names, marriage banns (Aufgebote); Burials (Begräbnisse) — name, date/place of death, age, cause of death, survivors; Confirmations (Konfirmationen, c. age 14 for Protestants); Family registers (Familienbücher) — especially common in Württemberg and Baden after 1808, listing a husband, wife, and all children with birth/confirmation/marriage/death dates in one record (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Catalog (search by parish under the 1871 place name); the Württemberg Lutheran regional church records are held by the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart and reachable via Archion (subscription) and the FamilySearch Catalog (Germany Church Records table of Protestant regional churches, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Duplicate church-book copies (Kirchenbuchduplikate, mostly beginning late 18th century) are held in central church or state archives, not the local parish.
- **Gaps:** No Württemberg-specific destruction was identified by any tool in this survey; the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648) destroyed many German church records generally, well before this 1780-1830 window, and WWII-era losses affected mainly eastern German Lutheran records, not Württemberg (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Language:** Protestant (Lutheran) registers in Germany were usually kept in German; Catholic registers mostly in Latin until the 1800s (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).

## Known record losses

added.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Württemberg, Germany (Lutheran church-book baptisms and marriages) (1780-1830)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** As a county (Grafschaft) from 1135; elevated to Duchy in 1495; the Kingdom of Württemberg from 1806. For FamilySearch Catalog purposes, German records are organized by the place name used at German unification in 1871 (place_search_all; Württemberg, Germany Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).
- **County seat / administrative center:** Stuttgart
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Holy Roman Empire to 1806, then the Kingdom of Württemberg (within the Confederation of the Rhine, then the German Confederation) through 1830; part of the modern state of Baden-Württemberg since 1952.
- **Population during period:** No Württemberg-specific figures were returned; FamilySearch's population tool gave only country-level Germany estimates for this period (c. 18.0 million in 1800 rising to c. 28.0 million by 1830 — Gapminder data via place_population).
- **Religious denominations:** Predominantly Lutheran (Evangelisch), with Catholic and Reformed minority populations; separate record series were kept by denomination (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Key historical events:** Napoleonic Wars reorganized the territory into the Kingdom of Württemberg (1806); areas west of the Rhine under French control saw civil registration introduced, but Württemberg itself (east of the Rhine) was not annexed and did not adopt civil registration in this period — church registers remained the primary vital-record system (Germany Civil Registration, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration).

## Boundary changes
- No boundary change affecting record jurisdiction occurred for Württemberg proper within 1780-1830; its status changed from Duchy to Kingdom (1806) without altering the underlying parish/county structure the FamilySearch Catalog uses (keyed to the 1871 Meyer's Gazetteer place names regardless of this period's status).
- Researchers should note the Catalog's 1871-era place names may differ from the 1780-1830 local terms for the same parish; always search the Catalog using the modern/1871 place string returned by place_search.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Württemberg is not listed among the areas where Napoleonic-period civil registration (1798-1815) was instituted, and it is not listed among the states that registered before the Empire-wide requirement; statewide civil registration for Württemberg therefore began only with the Empire-wide law of 1 January 1876 (Germany Civil Registration, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration). For 1780-1830, there is no civil-registration series to search.
- **What exists:** None for this window; civil birth/marriage/death registers (Standesamtsregister) begin only in 1876.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Lutheran (and Catholic/Reformed) church registers are the vital-record system for this period — see Church records below.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Lutheran (Evangelisch) churches began requiring registers around 1540; Catholic parish records were mandated in 1563; Reformed parishes mostly by 1650 (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Württemberg was predominantly Lutheran.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (Taufen) — infant's name, parents' names, legitimacy status, witnesses/godparents, baptism date, sometimes birth date and father's occupation; Marriages (Heiraten) — date, bride/groom names, sometimes ages, birthplaces, parents' names, marriage banns (Aufgebote); Burials (Begräbnisse) — name, date/place of death, age, cause of death, survivors; Confirmations (Konfirmationen, c. age 14 for Protestants); Family registers (Familienbücher) — especially common in Württemberg and Baden after 1808, listing a husband, wife, and all children with birth/confirmation/marriage/death dates in one record (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Catalog (search by parish under the 1871 place name); the Württemberg Lutheran regional church records are held by the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart and reachable via Archion (subscription) and the FamilySearch Catalog (Germany Church Records table of Protestant regional churches, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Duplicate church-book copies (Kirchenbuchduplikate, mostly beginning late 18th century) are held in central church or state archives, not the local parish.
- **Gaps:** No Württemberg-specific destruction was identified by any tool in this survey; the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648) destroyed many German church records generally, well before this 1780-1830 window, and WWII-era losses affected mainly eastern German Lutheran records, not Württemberg (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Language:** Protestant (Lutheran) registers in Germany were usually kept in German; Catholic registers mostly in Latin until the 1800s (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** collections_search and volume_search returned no Württemberg-specific census collection for 1780-1830; this survey did not confirm a state-level census of this period.
- **Other enumerations:** volume_search's summary lists a "Census" group of 378 digitized volumes matching this place/period search (266 browse-only); these were not examined individually in this survey and may mix other periods/places inside the search window.
- **Access:** Per the volume_search summary, most matched volumes in nearly every record-type group are majority browse-only (no name index) for this period.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** The volume_search summary lists Probate (198 volumes, 196 browse-only), Court (230 volumes, 228 browse-only), Wills (8 volumes, all browse-only), and Guardianship (51 volumes, all browse-only) for Württemberg in this period.
- **Testate or intestate:** Not established for a specific individual in this survey; both will (Testamente) and administration/guardianship (Vormundschaft) series exist per the volume counts above — check both.
- **Where held:** catalog_search found a Württemberg, Schwäbisch Hall, Probate Records, 1803-1929 collection (collections_search id 1475994); the German research-tips page notes 90% of the Württemberg population were dependent farmers whose land transactions were recorded in court records such as "Schuld- und Pfandprotokolle" (Germany Research Tips and Strategies, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).

### Land records
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed by this survey — the {Jurisdiction}_Land_and_Property page was not fetched; this guide does not state a land-distribution authority for Württemberg.
- **Types:** volume_search's summary lists a "Land" group of 19 volumes for this place/period, all browse-only.
- **Where held:** Not established beyond the volume count above; consult the FamilySearch Catalog directly for named towns.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Napoleonic Wars (Württemberg troops served in Napoleon's Grande Armée, including the 1812 Russian campaign).
- **Record types:** external_links_search returned Germany & Austria, Directories of Military and Marine Officers, 1500-1939 (Ancestry) and Germany and Austria, Military and Marine Unit Histories, 1760-1933 (Ancestry) as curated links covering this period.
- **Where held:** Per volume_search's summary, only 1 digitized "Military" volume matched this place/period search; this survey did not confirm dedicated online Württemberg military service/pension files for 1780-1830 beyond the Ancestry unit-history/officer-directory indexes above.

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** external_links_search returned a general BillionGraves Germany search and a "Germany Tombstones" index at genealogy.net (http://grabsteine.genealogy.net/landlist.php?lang=de), neither narrowed to Württemberg specifically.
- **Physical records:** Not established beyond the links above; this survey did not confirm sexton or burial-register holdings specific to a Württemberg parish.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** volume_search's summary lists only 6 "Newspapers" volumes matching Württemberg for this place/period, all browse-only; none were individually identified by title/date range in this survey.
- **Content value:** Per Germany Research Tips and Strategies, newspapers (Zeitungen, Amtsblätter) are named as a substitute source when church books no longer exist (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** external_links_search returned the Württemberg Emigration Index, 1808-1890 (Ancestry, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/3141/, also listed via GermanRoots at https://www.germanroots.com/wuerttemberg.html) and Auswanderung aus Südwestdeutschland, 1751-1920 (http://www.auswanderer-bw.de/auswanderer/index.php?sprache=de&suche=1), both overlapping this period.
- **Content note:** Per volume_search's summary, "Emigration" (658 volumes, all browse-only) and "Migration" (781 volumes, all browse-only) groups also matched this place/period; these are name-unindexed and must be browsed image by image.

### Tax records
- **Types:** volume_search's summary lists a "Tax" group of 100 volumes for this place/period, all browse-only. Germany Research Tips and Strategies names Steuerlisten/Steuerrollen (tax lists) as key substitutes when distinguishing identically named individuals or when church books are destroyed (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists were collected twice yearly and continued recording a household (often under the widow's name) after a head of household's death — useful where no civil registration exists for this period.

### Other record types
- **School records:** volume_search's summary lists only 2 "School" volumes for this place/period (browse-only); Germany Research Tips and Strategies also notes school-fee records ("Schülerverzeichnis") can help confirm paternity in illegitimate-birth cases (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Business/Reference:** volume_search's summary lists 13 "Business" and 1 "Reference" volume for this place/period.
- **Guild and citizenship records:** The research-tips page names Bürgerrolle/Bürgerbuch (citizenship rolls) and guild records (Innungslisten, Zunftbücher) as useful when a family's town of origin is unknown (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1971 (collection 3015626); Germany, Württemberg, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1818-1915 (collection 4132030); Germany Births and Baptisms, 1558-1898 (collection 1473000); Germany Marriages, 1558-1929 (collection 1473009) | Lutheran baptism/marriage/burial coverage spanning 1780-1830 | Free |
| Archion | Württemberg Lutheran regional church records, held by the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart (https://www.archion.de/de/archive-in-archion/baden-wuerttemberg/landeskirchliches-archiv-stuttgart/) | Direct digitized-image access to the Württemberg Lutheran church archive's own holdings | Subscription |
| Ancestry | Württemberg, Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1985 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61023); Germany Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1518-1921 (https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=61456); Württemberg, Germany Emigration Index, 1808-1890 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/3141/) | Lutheran BMB coverage and emigration indexing not all held at FamilySearch | Subscription |
| GenWiki (genealogy.net) | Portal:Württemberg (http://wiki-de.genealogy.net/Portal:W%C3%BCrttemberg) | Local research-community finding aids and indexes | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 16,120 digitized volumes matched Württemberg and 1780-1830 in volume_search; only the first 10 were individually detailed above (a first page), and the Catalog search returned 2,651 catalog hits of which only 25 were hydrated with detail — the rest were not examined.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart | Württemberg Evangelical (Lutheran) church records archive | Subscription digitization via Archion; direct correspondence per Germany Church Records guidance |
| Local parish (Pfarramt) | Original baptism, marriage, and burial registers still held by many parishes | Write in German per the German Letter Writing Guide (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/German_Letter_Writing_Guide) |
| State/central archives | Duplicate church-book copies (Kirchenbuchduplikate) from the late 18th century forward | Write or visit; see Germany Archives and Libraries |

- Civil registration does not exist for this period in Württemberg (begins only 1876), so there is nothing of that type to be online or otherwise.
- Per volume_search's summary, the large majority of matched Württemberg volumes for 1780-1830 across nearly every record-type group (Religious 2,715 of 7,013; Baptism 1,448 of 3,726; Religious Marriage 895 of 1,907; Probate 196 of 198; Court 228 of 230; Tax all 100; Land all 19; Migration/Emigration all) are browse-only images with no name index — present on FamilySearch but not searchable by name.
- Many original Württemberg parish registers remain held at the local Pfarramt or the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart rather than digitized anywhere online (Germany Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).

Germany Church Records states generally that "a large number of church records were destroyed in the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648)" (before this period) and that WWII caused destruction of "some church records, particularly Lutheran records, in areas that became modern Poland" (not Württemberg) — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records.
